### Highlights

- Displays whose capabilities string lies are now supported. Some MStar-based displays (for example the MSI MPG 274U) advertise standard MCCS input codes but only honor a private 1..=max index. DisplayMux now detects when the input a display is currently showing is missing from its own advertised list, switches to the index range the display reports, and labels those entries "Input N", so these displays can finally be switched.
- After writing an input, DisplayMux reads it back to confirm the display actually changed. A display that acknowledges the command without acting on it is now reported as a real failure instead of a false success notification.

### Dashboard state

- Each shared display remembers which host it was last confirmed switched to. The "Currently displayed" badge and "Switch to this host" buttons follow that state instead of always assuming the local computer is showing.
- The dashboard refreshes automatically after a switch completes; no manual refresh is needed.
- Dark theme colors were added for the display strip and local input rows.

### Fixes

- Fixed a transient DDC/CI read error during post-switch verification (for example "checksum mismatch") being reported as a failed switch that required a second click.

### Known limitations

- This release is signed with a new key and published from OmarHung/DisplayMuxAuto. The built-in updater on earlier versions cannot upgrade to it; download and install this version manually once.
- macOS cannot read or write DDC/CI on a connector that is not the display's active input. After switching away, switch back from the host currently shown or with the display's own buttons.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may require manual approval.
